scenario.recruiter: time-constrained independent recruiter reconciling contact clues across conversations and relationship contexts
scenario.trigger: A recruiter has a name or alias plus an email, phone, WeChat identifier, or profile URL and needs to attach new evidence without creating a duplicate person.
scenario.job_to_be_done: Use a source-backed identity clue to find the stable person, understand why the result matched, and deliberately bind the new source to the correct relationship.
scenario.success_condition: An unrelated entered name still resolves to the existing confirmed-handle owner, raw identity values are not returned or stored as display data, and a second person cannot be created from the same confirmed handle.
scenario.pressure_limit: The replay is synthetic and local; it does not measure a working recruiter's speed or error rate.

frozen_evidence: Database readback: one person, three active relationship contexts, six governed sources, and one source-linked masked confirmed email handle
12 backend test files and 71 tests passing

findings.observation: The Agent now shows compact source-backed match reasons and all returned candidates, and a confirmed handle reliably wins over an unrelated entered name. The runtime proof does not exercise two plausible people or persist a leave-unresolved identity case.
findings.evidence: The wrong-name replay returned exactly one existing person with Confirmed Email, masked hint, source-linked reason, all three relationship contexts, and a disabled new-person action.
findings.user_impact: Common alias and repeat-contact cases require less directory searching, but a true collision may still force the recruiter to stop and reconstruct identity outside the draft.
findings.recommendation: Seed two same-name people and conflicting or incomplete clues; expose only source-backed differentiators and persist leave unresolved as a resumable identity case.
findings.verification: The recruiter can compare two candidates, choose one or leave unresolved, reload, and resume without creating either a duplicate person or an unsupported merge.

findings.observation: The executable flow removes a concrete duplicate-identity failure mode, but no working-recruiter comparison establishes its frequency, time saving, or willingness to pay.
findings.evidence: The browser and database replay is local and synthetic.
findings.user_impact: The product value is technically credible but not yet commercial evidence.
findings.recommendation: Run a timed identity-binding comparison using consented recruiter cases and their current fallback.
findings.verification: Measure lookup time, duplicate rate, wrong-context corrections, abandonment, and reuse across at least five recruiter-owned cases.

strengths: The optional clue keeps the draft compact rather than turning it into a CRM form.
The recruiter sees exactly why a candidate matched and can inspect every existing relationship context.
A confirmed handle resolves aliases without treating a name as proof.
The first source and identity confirmation remain one deliberate workflow.
Refresh preserves the identity result and duplicate-prevention boundary.
missing_evidence: Two plausible same-name candidates with conflicting or incomplete handles.
Persisted unresolved identity review and Agent operation history.
Working-recruiter comparison against the current fallback.
open_questions: Which source-backed differentiators are sufficient for a recruiter to resolve a collision without exposing unnecessary personal data?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: A handle becomes confirmed only through an explicit recruiter decision tied to a governed contact-record source. Matching uses a normalized hash; directory results contain only a masked hint and source identifier. A confirmed handle cannot be assigned to a second person.
findings.evidence: Runtime database readback; raw-value absence assertion; identityHandles.test.ts conflict and minimization cases; wrong-name browser replay.
findings.user_impact: The system can explain deterministic identity narrowing without returning the raw clue or silently merging records.
findings.recommendation: Add a source-opening affordance with authorization checks and define expiry, revocation, and correction behavior for each handle type.
findings.verification: Confirm, revoke, correct, expire, and delete a handle source; lookup and every derived candidate reason must update or retract with no cross-context leakage.

findings.observation: The backend fails closed when a confirmed handle has another owner, while the Agent draft does not yet convert conflicting or multiple plausible matches into a durable unresolved case.
findings.evidence: IDENTITY_HANDLE_CONFIRMED_ELSEWHERE unit case; runtime new-person action disabled for an existing owner; no two-candidate runtime artifact.
findings.user_impact: The proven flow prevents corruption, but recovery from a real collision is not yet a resumable user workflow.
findings.recommendation: Persist candidate identifiers, masked reasons, ambiguity reasons, recruiter decision, and later correction as an identity-resolution case separate from person facts.
findings.verification: Exercise conflict, cancel, reload, later bind, later split, source deletion, and recompilation; no unresolved state may publish as a confirmed identity.

strengths: Raw identity values are transient inputs rather than directory or display data.
Match reasons distinguish name hints from stronger confirmed handles.
Confirmation authority remains with the recruiter and is source linked.
Second-owner creation fails closed in both UI and backend service boundaries.
No external contact, message, calendar, ATS, or CRM write is authorized.
The flow ranks work attention and identity evidence, never the person's worth or acceptance probability.
missing_evidence: Handle correction, expiry, revocation, and source-deletion runtime replay.
Recruiter comprehension testing for masking and provenance copy.
open_questions: Should every handle type share one masking policy, or should phone, WeChat, email, and public profile URLs have separate minimum-display rules?

affected_finding_result.prior_finding: The Agent did not show source-linked confirmed-handle match reasons before creation.
resolved: Optional email, phone, WeChat, and profile clue parsing
